_comment: Milestone A step 8 (ANCESTOR intersection resolver). Structures where the VENDORED RNApuzzler oracle (src/vienna_layout, plot_coords_puzzler_sibling_ancestor) does not terminate under a checkSiblingIntersections=1/checkAncestorIntersections=1/optimize=0 configuration. Generated the same way as hard_set_sibling_only_oracle_hangs.json (a hard per-structure multiprocessing timeout probe, 3.0s here, over the full benchmarks/hard_set.json, 450 structures) -- EMPTY: unlike the sibling-only combination (81/450 hang, see hard_set_sibling_only_oracle_hangs.json), the sibling-only infinite-loop failure mode is a restart of checkAndFixIntersections's outer while loop with NOTHING able to make progress (checkSiblings alone, when an intersecting pair's bounding wedges never overlap in angle-space, never applies a config change, so the restart re-runs against a byte-for-byte unchanged tree forever). With checkAncestorIntersections=1 also on, the ancestor pass runs BEFORE the sibling pass at every tree level on every restart and CAN make progress even when the sibling pass alone cannot (see resolve_internal.hpp's SiblingCheckResult doc comment and resolve_siblings.cpp's check_siblings doc comment for the full re-derivation) -- empirically, this breaks every one of the 450 hard_set structures' potential infinite loops, on this corpus. This file exists (rather than being omitted) so the parity harness (tests/test_native_parity.py) has a single, consistent mechanism (an exclusion list, even an empty one) across both resolver-combination test suites, and so a future corpus change that DOES reintroduce a hang has an obvious place to record it. Regenerate via a find_ancestor_hangs.py-style multiprocessing probe (scratchpad, not committed) if hard_set.json changes.
